description: Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled offers an unparalleled smoky flavor and succulent texture, making it a beloved Indian classic. Marinated in a rich blend of yogurt and aromatic spices, the chicken is cooked to perfection over hot coals, achieving a beautiful char and tender interior. This authentic recipe brings the vibrant tastes of India to your backyard grill, perfect for a memorable dinner.

ingredients.notes: bone-in, skinless, cut into large pieces

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken
instructions.text: Wash and pat dry the chicken pieces thoroughly. Make deep gashes on each piece to allow the marinade to penetrate. In a large bowl, combine 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tsp salt, and 1 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder. Rub this first marinade all over the chicken pieces and set aside for 15 minutes.

instructions.title: Prepare the Second Marinade
instructions.text: In a separate bowl, whisk together the thick yogurt, remaining ginger-garlic paste, remaining lemon juice, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, black pepper powder, remaining salt, mustard oil, and red food color (if using). Ensure the mixture is smooth and well combined.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: Add the chicken pieces with the first marinade into the bowl with the second marinade. Mix well, ensuring every piece is thoroughly coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or ideally overnight, for best flavor and tenderness.

instructions.title: Prepare the Charcoal Grill
instructions.text: About 30-45 minutes before grilling, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the charcoal to create a two-zone fire: one side with direct high heat and the other with indirect medium heat. The coals should be ash-gray and glowing hot.

instructions.title: Grill the Tandoori Chicken
instructions.text: Lightly oil the grill grates to prevent sticking. Place the marinated chicken pieces directly over the high heat zone. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side to get a nice char. Then, move the chicken to the indirect heat zone, close the lid, and cook for 20-25 minutes, turning occasionally, until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C) and the juices run clear.

instructions.title: Baste and Finish
instructions.text: During the last 5-7 minutes of cooking, you can baste the chicken with any remaining marinade or a mixture of oil and butter for extra moisture and flavor. Once cooked, remove the chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5 minutes before serving.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Arrange the Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken on a platter. Sprinkle generously with chaat masala, garnish with fresh chopped cilantro, and serve immediately with lemon wedges, mint chutney, or sliced onions. Enjoy this smoky, flavorful Indian delight!

tips: For truly authentic flavor, marinate the chicken for at least 8-12 hours. The longer the marination, the more tender and flavorful the chicken will be.
Maintain a consistent medium-high heat on your charcoal grill. Avoid flare-ups by trimming excess fat from chicken and moving pieces to indirect heat if needed.
Basting the chicken with a little melted butter or oil during the last few minutes of grilling helps keep it moist and adds a beautiful sheen and richness.
article:
Unleash the tantalizing aroma of a smoky, spiced masterpiece in your own backyard! If you've ever dreamt of recreating the magic of authentic Indian cuisine, look no further than Tandoori Chicken. But not just any Tandoori Chicken – we're talking about the truly incomparable **Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken**. This iconic dish, a staple of Indian dinner recipes, promises a burst of flavors and an unforgettable dining experience, all thanks to the unique char and tenderness imparted by open flame grilling. Get ready to transform your regular chicken into a culinary sensation that will have your taste buds singing.

## What is Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken?

Tandoori Chicken is a world-renowned Indian dish where chicken, marinated in yogurt and a vibrant blend of spices, is traditionally cooked in a tandoor – a cylindrical clay oven. The intense heat of the tandoor, fueled by charcoal or wood, gives the chicken its characteristic smoky flavor, crispy exterior, and incredibly juicy interior. When we talk about **Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken**, we're essentially bringing that authentic tandoor experience to your home grill. The direct heat and smoke from charcoal imbue the chicken with a depth of flavor that baking or pan-frying simply cannot replicate. The marinade, typically a rich concoction of yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, and a specific mix of Indian spices like turmeric, red chili powder, cumin, coriander, and garam masala, tenderizes the meat while infusing it with its signature reddish-orange hue and complex taste profile. It's more than just grilled chicken; it's a celebration of Indian spices and cooking techniques.

## Ingredients You'll Need for Tandoori Chicken

To embark on your journey to create the perfect Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken, gather these essential ingredients:

*   **For the Chicken:**
    *   2-3 lbs chicken pieces (thighs, drumsticks, or a whole cut-up chicken), skinless and bone-in for best flavor and juiciness.
    *   1 lemon, juiced
    *   1 tablespoon salt
*   **For the Marinade:**
    *   1 cup plain full-fat yogurt (Greek yogurt can be used for a thicker marinade)
    *   2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste (equal parts fresh ginger and garlic, crushed)
    *   1 tablespoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color and mild heat, or regular for more spice)
    *   1 tablespoon ground cumin
    *   1 tablespoon ground coriander
    *   1 teaspoon turmeric powder
    *   1 teaspoon garam masala
    *   1/2 teaspoon black pepper
    *   1 tablespoon mustard oil or vegetable oil
    *   1/2 teaspoon red food coloring (optional, but gives the classic vibrant color)
    *   Salt to taste (adjust after initial chicken salting)
*   **For Grilling:**
    *   Vegetable oil or melted butter for basting

The yogurt in the marinade acts as a tenderizer due to its acidity, breaking down the chicken fibers without making it tough. The spices are the heart of the dish, each contributing to the complex flavor. Mustard oil adds a pungent, authentic touch, but any neutral oil works.

## How to Make Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken: Step-by-Step

Creating this Indian masterpiece is simpler than you might think. Follow these steps for a truly delicious **Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken**:

1.  **Prepare the Chicken:** Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them dry. Using a sharp knife, make deep slits (2-3 per piece) on the chicken. This allows the marinade to penetrate deeply, ensuring maximum flavor and even cooking.
2.  **First Marinade (Pre-Marination):** In a large bowl, rub the chicken pieces with lemon juice and 1 tablespoon of salt. Let it rest for 15-20 minutes. This initial step helps to draw out moisture and further tenderize the chicken.
3.  **Prepare the Second Marinade:** In a separate bowl, combine the yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, ground cumin, ground coriander, turmeric powder, garam masala, black pepper, mustard oil (or vegetable oil), and red food coloring (if using). Mix everything until well combined and smooth. Taste and adjust salt if needed.
4.  **Marinate the Chicken:** Drain any excess liquid from the chicken. Add the chicken pieces to the yogurt-spice marinade, ensuring each piece is thoroughly coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or ideally overnight (up to 24 hours). The longer the marination, the more flavorful and tender your chicken will be.
5.  **Prepare Your Charcoal Grill:** About 30-45 minutes before you plan to cook, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the hot coals for direct medium-high heat. Once the coals are ash-gray and glowing, you're ready. Lightly oil your grill grates to prevent sticking.
6.  **Grill the Chicken:** Place the marinated chicken pieces directly over the hot coals. Cook for 20-30 minutes, turning every 5-7 minutes to ensure even cooking and prevent burning. Baste the chicken frequently with oil or melted butter, especially in the last 10 minutes of grilling. The chicken is done when it's beautifully charred on the outside, cooked through, and the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C).
7.  **Rest and Serve:** Once cooked, remove the chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5-10 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring moist and tender chicken.

## Pro Tips for the Best Charcoal Tandoori Chicken

Achieving that perfect, restaurant-quality **Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken** is all about attention to detail.

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The longer the chicken soaks in the spicy yogurt, the more tender and flavorful it will become. Overnight is truly best.
*   **Bone-in, Skinless Chicken:** While boneless chicken works, bone-in pieces impart more flavor and stay juicier. Removing the skin allows the marinade to directly penetrate the meat and prevents a greasy texture.
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Grill:** Cook in batches if necessary. Overcrowding lowers the grill temperature and can lead to steaming rather than grilling, preventing that desirable char.
*   **Maintain Grill Temperature:** Keep an eye on your charcoal. You want consistent medium-high heat. If it gets too hot, move chicken to a cooler part of the grill or raise the grate. If it cools down, add a few fresh coals.
*   **Baste for Moisture and Flavor:** Regular basting with oil or butter during the grilling process keeps the chicken moist and adds another layer of flavor and richness.
*   **Internal Temperature:** Always use a meat thermometer to ensure the chicken is cooked to a safe internal temperature of 165°F (74°C). This prevents overcooking and dryness.
*   **Fresh Ingredients:** Use fresh ginger-garlic paste and good quality spices for the most vibrant flavor.

## Serving Suggestions for Tandoori Chicken

**Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken** is a star dish that deserves to be paired with equally delicious accompaniments. Here are some classic Indian dinner recipes to complete your meal:

*   **Naan or Roti:** Warm, fluffy naan bread or whole wheat roti are perfect for scooping up the chicken and its juices.
*   **Mint Chutney:** A refreshing mint and coriander chutney provides a tangy, cooling contrast to the spicy chicken.
*   **Onion Salad:** Simple sliced red onions, often marinated in lemon juice and a pinch of chili powder, add a crisp, pungent bite.
*   **Lemon Wedges:** A squeeze of fresh lemon juice over the hot chicken brightens all the flavors.
*   **Cucumber Raita:** A cool yogurt dip with grated cucumber and a hint of cumin is excellent for balancing the heat.
*   **Basmati Rice:** A side of fragrant plain or jeera (cumin) basmati rice can also complement the meal beautifully.
*   **Fresh Salad:** A simple green salad with a light vinaigrette can add freshness.

## Variations and Frequently Asked Questions

*   **Can I use boneless chicken?** Yes, boneless chicken (thighs or breasts) can be used. Adjust cooking time accordingly; boneless pieces will cook faster (15-20 minutes).
*   **What if I don't have a charcoal grill?** While a charcoal grill provides the most authentic flavor, you can use a gas grill (preheat to medium-high) or even bake it in the oven (at 400°F/200°C for 30-40 minutes, finishing under the broiler for char). However, for that true smoky essence, **Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken** is unmatched.
*   **Can I make it less spicy?** Absolutely! Reduce the amount of red chili powder or omit it entirely if you prefer a milder flavor. Kashmiri chili powder offers a beautiful color with less heat.
*   **Is Tandoori Chicken healthy?** Yes, it's a relatively healthy dish. It's high in lean protein, low in fat (especially if skinless), and packed with beneficial spices.
*   **Can I prepare the marinade ahead of time?** Yes, the marinade can be made a day or two in advance and stored in the refrigerator. This can be a great time-saver for busy weeknights.
*   **Can I freeze marinated chicken?** Yes, you can freeze the marinated chicken for up to a month. Thaw it completely in the refrigerator before grilling.

Bringing the vibrant flavors of India to your dinner table has never been easier or more rewarding. The rich, smoky aroma and succulent taste of **Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken** make it a truly special dish, perfect for family dinners or entertaining guests. So fire up your grill, embrace the spices, and get ready to enjoy one of the most beloved Indian dinner recipes right in your own home!
